instructions:
1. Set the suspension trainer handles to about knee height. Lie on your back and place your heels in the handles with your legs extended.
2. Rest your arms on the floor at your sides for support.
3. Lift your hips off the floor and bend your knees, pulling your heels toward your glutes.
4. Slowly extend your legs back to the start with control, keeping your hips raised.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Drive through your hamstrings and squeeze your glutes to keep your hips high.
2. Keep your core braced so your lower back does not sag.
3. Exhale as you curl in, inhale as you extend out.
4. Move slowly to control the unstable straps.

instructions:
1. Set the suspension trainer handles to about knee height and place your feet in the handles.
2. Assume a plank position with your hands directly under your shoulders and arms extended.
3. Brace your core and keep a straight line from head to heels.
4. Drive one knee toward your chest, then quickly switch legs in a running motion.
5. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your hips level and core tight to control the unstable straps.
2. Position your shoulders directly over your hands.
3. Start slow and build speed as your coordination improves.
4. Breathe steadily throughout the movement.

instructions:
1. Set the suspension trainer handles to about knee height and place your feet in the handles.
2. Assume a plank position with your hands slightly wider than shoulder-width under your shoulders.
3. Brace your core and keep a straight line from head to heels.
4. Keeping your legs straight, lift your hips toward the ceiling into an inverted V.
5. Slowly lower your hips back to the plank position with control.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Lift with your core rather than pulling with your arms.
2. Keep your legs straight and shoulders over your hands.
3. Start with a smaller range and increase as you get stronger.
4. Exhale as you lift your hips, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Set the suspension trainer handles to about knee height. Sit on the floor with your legs extended and place your feet in the handles.
2. Position your hands on the floor at your sides, fingers pointing forward.
3. Press through your hands and lift your hips into a reverse plank, forming a straight line from head to heels.
4. Lower your hips toward the floor with control, stopping just before they touch.
5. Press through your hands and lift back to the reverse plank.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Squeeze your glutes hard at the top to keep your hips high.
2. Keep your core tight so your hips do not sag.
3. Move with a steady, controlled tempo.
4. Exhale as you lift your hips, inhale as you lower.

instructions:
1. Set the suspension trainer handles to an overhead position. Stand underneath and grasp them with an overhand grip, shoulder-width apart.
2. Bend and cross your legs for stability and hang with arms extended.
3. Pull your shoulder blades down, then drive your elbows down and back, lifting your chest toward the handles.
4. Pull until your chest is close to the handles.
5. Lower yourself with control until your arms are fully extended.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Initiate by depressing your shoulder blades before bending your elbows.
2. Keep your core tight to stop your body from swinging.
3. Start with fewer reps and build up as your strength improves.
4. Exhale as you pull up, inhale as you lower.
